title: SDK Lazy-Validate + Stream-Commit PRD (sketch)
body:
Context:
This is a working sketch for a developer-facing surface that makes long-running streaming requests (with optional tool calls and structured outputs) easy to integrate while keeping server-side guarantees about commit points/persistence and observability. The core idea: allow SDK clients to lazily validate structured payloads as they arrive and explicitly commit a stream when the app has verified satisfiability, while still offering resumability and autosave semantics for unreliable networks.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Customers building multi-step assistants (search+tool orchestration + multi-turn generation) need a predictable way to: (1) see partial structured results early (for UX), (2) perform validations or local enrichment (e.g., run a quick safety check, call a tool), and (3) atomically commit the final output so downstream systems treat it as canonical.
- Current streaming output model gives partial tokens/frames but does not present a clear validation/commit API. Engineers end up reimplementing fragile client-side checkpoints or overfetching.

Goals (MVP):
1) SDK surface: provide a small set of primitives for incremental reception + lazy validation + explicit commit/abort.
2) Structured frame model: define compact frame types for "partial-entity", "proposal", "tool-call", "validation-error", and "commit-marker".
3) Resumability: resume interrupted streams from last acknowledged commit-safe snapshot.
4) Observability: emit telemetry events for frame receipts, validation passes/fails, tool-call latency and commit times.
5) Backwards compatibility: default to current streaming token events if the client opts out.

Non-goals: server-side long-running transaction semantics, replacing the Console's rollouts, heavy on-chain persistence guarantees (we rely on commit markers + customer choice).

High-level flow (developer view):
1) Client opens a streaming call: createStream(requestPayload, {session_id, resume_token?}).
2) Redwood server streams frames (JSONL-like compact frames) containing partial structured pieces and tool call intents.
3) SDK exposes onFrame(callback) where callback receives typed frames. App can run lightweight validation locally or call SDK.verifyFrame(frame) which runs a quick schema check + optional server quick-check.
4) When app determines the output is acceptable it calls stream.commit({meta}) which sends a commit intent to Redwood and returns a commit-ack event when durable. Alternatively stream.abort() discards the in-progress result.
5) If network drops before commit, client can call createStream(..., {resume_token}) to continue from last saved snapshot and re-evaluate pending frames.

Frame examples (compact text representation used on wire):
- Partial entity frame: {"t":"pe","id":"p1","schema":"contact_v1","data":"{...}"}  // t=type shorthand
- Proposal frame (human-facing plain text suggestion): {"t":"pr","id":"r1","text":"Draft reply...","confidence":0.84}
- Tool call intent: {"t":"tc","id":"tc1","tool":"search_v2","args":"{\"q\":\"pricing redwood inference\"}"}
- Validation result: {"t":"vr","id":"v1","ok":false,"errors":["missing.phone"]}
- Commit marker (server): {"t":"cm","commit_id":"c-20250203-xy","durable":false}  // later replaced by durable:true ack

SDK ergonomics (JS pseudo-API sketch):
const s = await Redwood.stream.start({model: "rwd-short", prompt, sessionId});
s.on('frame', (f) => { // typed frame switch
  if (f.t === 'pe') renderPreview(f.data);
  if (f.t === 'tc') sdk.tools.exec(f.tool, f.args).then(res => s.feedToolResult(f.id, res));
  if (f.t === 'vr') showValidation(f.errors);
});

// app decides to validate locally, optionally ask server quick-validate
const ok = await s.validate({frameId: 'p1', mode: 'local+quick'});
if (ok) await s.commit({tags: ['user-signed','release-1']});
// commit returns when acknowledged durable=true or returns a commit token for async ack

Design details and tradeoffs:
- Lazy-validate vs server-validate: default validate() runs local schema checks against the frame payload (fast). An optional server quick-validate RPC can be used when the app needs Redwood to check cross-frame consistency. Quick-validate is best-effort and not blocking commit.
- Commit semantics: commit() is idempotent and returns a commit_id. SDK shows a transient state (committing) until server sets durable:true. We surface a commit event with commit_id and timestamps.
- Aborting: abort() signals the server to drop any provisional routing for the session. Not a guarantee of immediate deletion (backend GC window). Documented in API.
- Resumption: resume_token is a lightweight opaque token tied to the session and last durable commit. We avoid exposing internals; SDK persists resume_token in local storage if opt-in.
- Tool calls: tool-call frames are first-class; SDK exposes exec() helpers with built-in timeout and retry policies. Tool results are fed back into the stream as regular frames for the model to continue generation.

Observability requirements:
- Emit events: frame.received, validation.request, validation.result, toolcall.request, toolcall.result, commit.initiated, commit.ack, resume.attempt, resume.success, abort.request.
- Console: surface per-session timeline view with frame types and time delta to commit. Add filter for validation failures to aid regressions.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Reduced customer code doing custom checkpointing by 60% in pilot accounts (instrument via support threads / onboarding surveys).
- Mean-time-to-commit under good networks < 2s for commit ack (Durable ack by server within SLA).
- <2% accidental double-commits observed in pilot.
- Tool-call roundtrip telemetry available in Console for pilot customers.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (internal): implement minimal frame parser + commit API in SDK + backend accept/ack path behind feature flag (2 sprints).
- Phase 1 (pilot): enable for 3 internal teams + 2 external early customers, collect UX feedback and observe telemetry (4-6 weeks).
- Phase 2 (public beta): opt-in via request parameter; docs + sample app + migration notes (2 months).
- Phase 3 (GA): on by default with migration window and detailed SLA docs.

Developer docs & samples to ship in pilot:
- Quickstart: "Preview + Commit" (3 file sample app showing tool call, local validation and commit)
- Migration guide: mapping from older streaming token model to new frame model
- SDK cookbooks: common patterns (safety-first, optimistic-commit, offline-first)

Open questions / TODOs:
- durability SLA: what is acceptable ack latency for GA? (prod-sre input needed)
- resume_token rotation / lifetime: default TTL? encryption expectations? (security review)
- server quick-validate cost model: billable RPC? free-tier? (finance & pricing)
- SDK persistence location for resume_token on mobile (secure storage decisions)
- UX for partial frames on mobile with flaky network (bandwidth heuristics)

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally lightweight; aim is to remove friction for multi-step apps while keeping control in customer hands.
- We should align with Dedicated/Private semantics (commit -> store in customer-owned artifact if Private).
- Handoff to Console team: add an event schema and a per-session timeline widget (ask @Hannah Ruiz to take point).

Immediate next steps:
- Engineering: spike wire format and server ack flow (ENG-3214).
- SDK: prototype JS surface and a tiny Python parity library for the pilot.
- Product: pick 2 internal pilot teams (search assistant, invoice automation) and schedule integration tests.
